summary: Defines a SIP private header field, P-User-Database, used in the 3GPP IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS). It gives registrars and proxy servers the address of the database holding the user profile for the user who made a request. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A sticky note on a letter that says, the file about this person is in cabinet number such-and-such.

subtitle: A SIP header that tells the next 3GPP IMS server which user database to ask, saving a repeat lookup.

tldr.problem: In a 3GPP IMS network with several user databases (HSSs), the I-CSCF and then the S-CSCF each ask a locator function which HSS holds the user's profile, so the locator is consulted twice per request.
tldr.mechanism: The I-CSCF adds a P-User-Database header carrying the HSS address as a Diameter URI to the request it sends on, and the S-CSCF reads it, contacts that HSS directly and removes the header.
tldr.outcome: This shortens registration and handling of requests to unregistered users, and reduces load on the locator function. It is meant only for use inside 3GPP IMS networks.

facts.label: Value
facts.value: A Diameter URI in angle brackets

today: RFC 4457 is an Informational document, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The header was registered with the IANA as stated in the text, and its scope remains limited to 3GPP IMS networks.

sections.title: The Two IMS Scenarios
sections.content:
The 3GPP IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) uses SIP as its main signalling protocol. The RFC describes two situations in which several proxies handling a request must consult the same user database.

In the first, a user registers. A REGISTER request goes from the user agent to its outbound proxy, the P-CSCF, then to the I-CSCF in the home domain. The I-CSCF asks the user database, the Home Subscriber Server (HSS), to choose the registrar, the S-CSCF. The S-CSCF then has to contact the same HSS to fetch the user profile. These interfaces use Diameter and are called Cx.

In the second, a request arrives for a user who is not registered. The I-CSCF consults the HSS to pick an S-CSCF. If the user were registered, the S-CSCF would already know the HSS from registration. Since the user is not, it has to find out again.

When a domain has several HSSs, each serving certain users, a Diameter redirect agent called the Subscription Locator Function (SLF) tells a caller which HSS to use, over the Dx interface. As a result the SLF is consulted twice per REGISTER and twice per request to an unregistered user: first by the I-CSCF, later by the S-CSCF.
sections.eli5: A big office has many filing rooms, and a receptionist who knows which room holds each person's file. Right now two different clerks both ask the receptionist about the same person. That is a waste of time.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.content:
From these scenarios the RFC derives three requirements. First, optimize registration in the 3GPP IMS by reducing the time it takes a user agent to register. Second, optimize the handling of incoming requests to unregistered users by reducing the time it takes a domain to handle them. Third, improve the scalability of SLFs by reducing the traffic an SLF has to handle.

The idea behind all three is that if the I-CSCF already knows the HSS and passes that address on, the S-CSCF can contact the HSS directly and skip the SLF.
sections.eli5: The goal is simple: do it faster, and stop bothering the receptionist with the same question twice.

sections.title: The P-User-Database Header Field
sections.content:
The new header field, P-User-Database, can be added to requests routed from an I-CSCF to an S-CSCF. It contains the address of the HSS that handles the user who generated the request. Its value is a Diameter URI in angle brackets, followed by optional generic parameters.

The syntax is given in ABNF. DiameterURI comes from RFC 3588, and the tokens HCOLON, LAQUOT, RAQUOT and generic-param come from RFC 3261.
sections.eli5: The header is the sticky note. It holds one address: where to find the file for this person.

sections.title: Applicability and Scope
sections.content:
Under RFC 3427, P-headers have limited applicability, so their specifications must state their useful scope and why they are unsuitable for general Internet use. This header is intended for 3GPP IMS networks only. It travels between two proxies, the I-CSCF and the S-CSCF, in the same administrative domain, which share a common frame of reference to the user database. The I-CSCF inserts the header and the S-CSCF removes it before routing the request further.

On the general Internet there are typically no proxies querying a user database between the user agent sending a REGISTER and the registrar, so the header does not seem useful there.
sections.eli5: The sticky note is only for two clerks in the same office. The second clerk takes it off before passing the letter on, and it makes no sense outside that office.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The header is meant for an environment where elements are trusted and attackers cannot reach the messages between them. Traffic protection is sometimes done with IPsec and sometimes by physically protecting the network, and either way the integrity and confidentiality of the header are ensured.

There is a slight risk if the header leaves the administrative domain where it was created. No user-sensitive information would leak, but it could reveal operator network topology beyond what SIP messages normally disclose. Operators therefore need to remove the header before sending requests to another administrative domain.

The header field has been registered by the IANA in the Header Fields subregistry of the SIP Parameters registry.
sections.eli5: The note could tell outsiders how the office is laid out, so it must be taken off before a letter leaves the building.

data.title: P-User-Database
data.code:
P-User-Database     = "P-User-Database" HCOLON database
                      *( SEMI generic-param )
database            = LAQUOT DiameterURI RAQUOT

P-User-Database: <aaa://host.example.com;transport=tcp>
